animations.help: Instead of the VU meters, the Now Playing screen can show a CD, a CD changer, a vinyl record or a cassette turning with the music. The button next to the clock shows it full screen.

uiMotion.help: How much the screen moves when you touch it. The movement is short and stops by itself, so it costs the graphics chip next to nothing; turn it down if you prefer the interface to stand still.

optionHelp.full: Recommended — buttons give way under a finger, panels slide in
optionHelp.reduced: The same movements, twice as quick
optionHelp.none: Nothing moves: everything changes at once

playback.help: Playback options applied to the active player: track transitions (crossfade/gapless) and volume normalisation (ReplayGain).
playback.noPlayer: No active player found. Start playback or check the Lyrion connection.
playback.fixedVolumeHelp: Bypasses the player's digital volume control entirely — output is always at 100%. Required for bit-perfect playback; turn it off to use the on-screen volume slider again.
playback.vuMeterHelp: The VU dial in the "now playing" screen updates live with the audio level. Turn it off to reduce GPU load on more limited hardware.
playback.vuStyleHelp: The look of the meters in the "now playing" screen.
playback.autoExpandHelp: When a song starts playing, automatically open the fullscreen now-playing view after this many seconds. It only opens once per song — if you navigate away yourself, it stays put.

dsp.help: Optional digital signal processing: a parametric equalizer and headphone crossfeed applied to all playback.
dsp.warning: Turning DSP on disables bit-perfect playback (audio is resampled and DSD/DoP pass-through is bypassed). Leave it off for critical listening with an external DAC.
dsp.unavailable: DSP engine not installed on this device yet. It is set up automatically on the next system update (requires an internet connection).
dsp.noBands: No EQ bands. Add one to boost or cut a frequency.
dsp.roomCorrectionPresent: Filter loaded: {filename}. Upload a new one any time below, or run the guided measurement.
dsp.roomCorrectionMissing: No filter loaded yet. Upload a WAV/TXT convolution filter (REW/rePhase) below, or run the guided measurement.

roomcorr.title: Guided room correction
roomcorr.intro: The appliance plays a test sweep, records it with a USB measurement microphone and automatically generates the correction filter for this room.
roomcorr.req1: Connect a USB measurement microphone (e.g. miniDSP UMIK-1).
roomcorr.req2: Place the microphone at the listening position, at ear height.
roomcorr.req3: Set a normal listening volume and keep the room quiet during the measurement.
roomcorr.position: When you're ready, start: you'll hear a sweep of about 10 seconds.
roomcorr.noMic: No USB microphone detected. Connect one and reopen the wizard.
roomcorr.keepQuiet: Keep the room quiet until the measurement is done.
roomcorr.error: Measurement failed. Check the microphone and volume, then try again.

remote.help: A remote control works the whole interface: the arrows move the highlight, OK presses whatever the highlight is on, and the play, volume and back keys do what they say. A USB remote — the kind with a little receiver you plug in — works the moment you plug it in. A Bluetooth one has to be paired here first.
remote.keysBody: Arrows move the highlight, OK presses. Back closes what is open, or goes back a step. Home returns to the library. The menu key opens the same menu a long press on a row opens. Play, previous, next, volume and mute do what they say.
remote.none: No remote connected. Plug in the receiver of a USB remote, or pair a Bluetooth one below.
remote.noneYet: No remote yet. Add one with the button above, or plug in the receiver of a USB one: it works straight away.
remote.keysPageSub: See what each key sends and give it another job
remote.mineHint: Only needed for a remote that introduces itself as a keyboard, an air mouse for instance: those get the play and volume keys only, so typing on a real keyboard keeps working. Say this one is yours and every key of it is listened to — and what you set on it does not touch the keyboard.
remote.testHint: The next key you press is only shown here and does nothing else: you see what your remote really sends and can give that key another job. Then the remote works the screen again.
remote.pressAKey: Press a key on the remote…
remote.assignFailed: That key could not be set
remote.btHelp: Put the remote in pairing mode first — usually holding a key until its light blinks — then search.

pair.title: Add a remote

how.firetv: Hold the Home key (⌂) until the light at the top blinks.
how.xiaomi: Hold the ⋮⋮⋮ key and the ○ key together for 7–8 seconds, until the light blinks.
how.g20s: Hold OK and Back together for 5–7 seconds, until the light blinks.

pair.wait: Then leave it near the device: it is found and connected by itself.

uiResolution.help: On large screens the interface is drawn at full panel resolution, which keeps the graphics chip busy. Rendering it lower and letting the screen enlarge it makes everything much smoother, at the cost of some sharpness.

optionHelp.auto: Recommended — lowers the resolution only on screens that need it
optionHelp.native: Sharpest picture, heaviest on the graphics chip

uiResolution.restartWarning: The interface will close and reopen after a few seconds. Playback is not interrupted.

uiRefresh.help: Both the screen scaling and the interface's own redraws are tied to the panel's refresh rate, so lowering it reduces graphics-chip load — measured at roughly 40% less on this hardware. The needle/level movements stay smooth; fast animations may look very slightly less fluid.
uiRefresh.monitorDisclaimer: If the connected monitor doesn't support a lower refresh rate, switching won't have any effect — no visual difference and no reduction in graphics-chip load either.
uiRefresh.unsupported: This screen does not offer a lower refresh rate to switch to.

cdRip.help: How an audio CD is copied into the library. Every row applies at once.
cdRip.enableText: Detect discs and offer to rip them
cdRip.targetHelp: A folder inside a writable music source (internal or USB disk, writable network share). Albums land there as Artist/Album.
cdRip.targetUnset: Not set: the only writable source, or asked at rip time
cdRip.targetBad: Not available right now (disk unplugged or share not mounted)
cdRip.prefixHelp: A folder inside the default target folder that every ripped album goes into, chosen from the folder browser; none to rip straight into the target.
cdRip.prefixNeedsTarget: Set the default target folder first.
cdRip.prefixOutside: The prefix must be a folder inside the default target folder.
cdRip.autoStartHelp: Start by itself when a disc is inserted, into the default folder.
cdRip.wavHelp: WAV files carry no tags and no ReplayGain; cover and log are still saved next to them.
cdRip.retriesHelp: A track is read again until two reads agree.
cdRip.preEmphasisHelp: Early CDs with pre-emphasis: a tag lets the player correct it, the filter corrects the audio itself.

clean_names.label: File naming
clean_names.text: Clean up all special & non ASCII characters

log_file.label: Log file
log_file.text: Save ripping log file to the album folder

cdRip.speedHelp: Slower reads a worn disc more reliably and keeps the drive quieter.
cdRip.offsetHelp: Read offset in samples, as AccurateRip lists it for this drive. Calibrate looks it up online and sets it.
cdRip.offsetInvalid: The offset must be a whole number.
cdRip.ejectHelp: For a drive without its own button: ejects the disc whenever a rip is not running.

playerEnabled.label: Player
playerEnabled.help: Turn the player itself off for a server-only unit — Lyrion Music Server and everything else keeps running, this device just never plays audio locally. Useful for a box in a closet driving other players elsewhere.
playerEnabled.offWarning: This device will stop playing audio locally. Lyrion Music Server and remote control keep working.

lyrion.skinUnset: No skin chosen yet — the web player still uses Lyrion's stock look. Pick one to switch.
lyrion.skinFailed: Could not apply the skin. Check the network connection and try again.
lyrion.libraryHelp: What the music server has indexed. Refresh after adding or moving music by hand; the sources page does it on its own when a source changes.
lyrion.metaHelp: Credits, biographies and album details from MusicBrainz and Wikipedia. To find them, the device sends the names of your albums and artists to those sites.
lyrion.metaPrefetch: Prepare the whole library in the background
lyrion.metaPrefetchHelp: Album pages then open with everything already there. The device looks up one album at a time, slowly.
lyrion.metaWhereHelp: Change this and what has already been downloaded moves there — nothing is downloaded again.
lyrion.metaWhereAway: The disk you chose is not connected. For now the information is kept on this device; plug the disk back in and it goes back to it.
lyrion.metaNoNetwork: A network folder cannot hold it
lyrion.metaMoveFailed: The information could not be moved

sources.help: Add your music folders: USB sticks/drives (auto-mounted), network (SMB) or local folders. Changes take effect right away.

audio.help: Choose the playback device (DAC). The selection is saved and kept across reboots. DSD playback is bit-perfect: native when the DAC accepts it that way, DoP otherwise.
audio.advancedHint: Each row applies right away and restarts the player for a moment. Automatic is right for nearly every DAC.
audio.dsdDetectedNative: This DAC declares native DSD. DoP wraps the same bits in PCM frames, usually up to DSD128. Convert to PCM is for outputs with no DSD at all, such as HDMI.
audio.dsdDetectedDop: This DAC does not declare native DSD, so Automatic uses DoP. Convert to PCM is for outputs with no DSD at all, such as HDMI.
audio.dsdDetectedPcm: This output is not a USB DAC (HDMI or the built-in audio), so Automatic converts DSD to PCM. Choose DoP only if a DAC that takes DoP is connected to it.
audio.dsdDelayLabel: Pause when switching between PCM and DSD
audio.maxRateHelp: Anything above it is resampled by Lyrion before it reaches the player. Automatic lets the DAC say.
audio.volumeHelp: The volume in Lyrion moves the DAC's own control and the bits stay untouched. Off: software volume, bit-perfect at 100%.
audio.volumeNoMixer: This output has no hardware volume control.
audio.alsaBufferHelp: For DACs that drop out or crackle.
audio.streamBufferHelp: More music kept in memory ahead of playback, for a slow network or disk.
audio.realtimeHelp: The output thread runs ahead of everything else on the device.
audio.extraHint: Anything else squeezelite accepts, on one line, without quotes. The options handled above are refused here.

msg.confirmShutdown: Are you sure you want to shut down the system?

netCheck.openHelp: Finds where the connection stops: cable or Wi-Fi, router, internet or the update server.
netCheck.help: Osmium checks, one step at a time, whether it can reach the update server, and tells you where it stops.
netCheck.running: Checking… it takes at most half a minute.
netCheck.failed: The check could not start: the device's service did not answer.

err.noLink: Not connected to any network: check the cable or the Wi-Fi.
err.noAddress: Connected, but it has no address yet.
err.noDhcp: Connected, but the router did not give it an address.
err.weakSignal: Weak Wi-Fi signal: move it closer to the router or use a cable.
err.noGateway: The network did not say which router to use.
err.noPing: The router ignores ping, but it is there and working.
err.packetLoss: Some messages to the router get lost ({loss}%).
err.blockedIps: Direct connections are blocked, but the update server can be reached.
err.dns: Names cannot be looked up: the DNS server does not answer.
err.dnsPartial: Some names cannot be looked up.
err.clockOff: The clock is off by {time}: secure connections may fail.
err.clockWrong: The clock is wrong: secure connections fail.
err.fallback: The main server does not answer, but a backup does: updates still work.
err.rateLimited: GitHub is refusing requests for a while (too many).
err.badManifest: The server answered with something unexpected.
err.tlsCert: Security certificate refused: check the clock.

verdict.ok: All good: the device reaches the update server.
verdict.warn: It works, with a caveat: see the steps in yellow.
verdict.link: The problem is the device's own connection: check the cable or the Wi-Fi.
verdict.router: The problem is between the device and the router: restart the router and check the cable or the Wi-Fi.
verdict.internet: The router answers but does not reach the internet: the problem is the router or your internet provider.
verdict.dns: The internet works but names cannot be looked up: restart the router, or set other DNS servers in the network settings.
verdict.clock: The clock is wrong and secure connections fail: check the time zone and restart the device.
verdict.ota: Your internet works: it is the update server that does not answer right now. Try again later; if it keeps happening, a filter on your network may be blocking it.
verdict.download: The update server answers but the download does not start: try again later, or check for filters on your network.

verdictWarn.link: It works, but the Wi-Fi signal is weak: move the device closer to the router or use a cable.
verdictWarn.router: It works, but the link to the router drops now and then: if the music stops, check the Wi-Fi or the cable.
verdictWarn.internet: It works: your network blocks some connections, but not the ones updates need.
verdictWarn.dns: It works, but some addresses cannot be found: if updates fail, restart the router.
verdictWarn.clock: It works, but the device's clock is a little off: check the time zone.
verdictWarn.ota: It works: the main server does not answer, so the device uses the backup one.

connectivity.lanWired: Connected by cable, but the internet is not reachable

welcome.title: Let’s try the remote
welcome.body: I will ask for one key at a time: press the right one and we move on. Press {okKey} to start.

arrows.title: The spotlight
arrows.body: The gold outline shows what is selected. Move it with the arrows: try up, down, left and right.

ok.title: Opening
ok.body: Press {okKey} to open what is selected, as if you touched it.

menu.title: The menu
menu.body: Press {menuKey}: it opens the actions of the selected item, like the queue and favourites.

back.title: Going back
back.body: Press {backKey} to go back to the previous screen.

albums.title: In the album grid
albums.body: The spotlight is on an album: press → to move to its play button. OK there plays the album straight away.

az.title: The A–Z index
az.body: Press → again to reach the index, then ↓ or ↑ to pick a letter: the list jumps there.

coverflow.title: Cover Flow
coverflow.body: Here ← and → flip through the albums. Try both.

coverflowPlay.title: Play in Cover Flow
coverflowPlay.body: Press ↓ to move to the play button of the album in front. OK on the cover opens the album instead.

home.title: Home
home.body: Press {homeKey}: from any screen it takes you back to the library.

volume.title: The volume
volume.body: Press volume + or volume −. It works from every screen.

play.title: Play and pause
play.body: Press {playKey} to pause the music or start it again.

player.title: The player
player.body: Press {playerKey} to open and close the full-screen player.

done.title: Well done, you know it all
done.body: The key map and this practice are in Settings → Remote control. Press {okKey} to finish.

firetv.KEY_KPENTER: the key in the middle of the ring
firetv.KEY_SEARCH: the blue key at the top

xiaomi.KEY_SELECT: the key in the middle of the ring

welcome.title: Welcome to Osmium Sound
welcome.body: A quick tour of the screen: what is where, and what a touch does. It takes a minute, and you can see it again from Settings → System info.

miniPlayer.title: What is playing
miniPlayer.body: The left side always shows the current track: cover, title, play and skip keys, shuffle and repeat, the volume. Touch the artist or the album name to open their page.

expand.title: The big player
expand.body: This arrow opens the full Now Playing screen, with the VU meters or an animation. Swipe it down, or touch the arrow at its top left, to come back.

tabs.title: Music, Radio, Apps, Discover, Settings
tabs.body: The tabs at the top: your library, internet radios, the Lyrion apps, music to discover, and the settings of the appliance. The power key is in the corner, and next to it the network icon: touch it to see whether the internet is reachable.

library.title: Your library
library.body: Search the whole library from the box, or browse by artists, albums, genres, years, composers, folders and playlists. In any list, a long press on a row opens its menu: play next, add to the queue, favourites.

albumList.title: The albums
albumList.body: Every album of the library, with its cover. A touch opens the album, the play button on the card plays it right away. Type in the box to filter, or jump with the letters on the right.

longPress.title: Hold to get the menu
longPress.body: Keep a finger on an album, a track, an artist or a playlist for a moment: its menu opens, like this one. Play next, add to the queue, save among the favourites, go to the artist.

coverFlow.title: Cover Flow
coverFlow.body: The same albums as a row of covers to flip through: drag with a finger, turn the mouse wheel, touch a cover at the side, hold the arrows, or slide the knob below. Switch between grid and Cover Flow with the button in the crumb bar, or in Settings → Library.

npLeft.title: Clock, full screen, looks
npLeft.body: The clock starts the screensaver. Next to it: full screen for the meters or the animation, then the two choosers: which VU meters, which animation (a CD, a record, a cassette).

npRight.title: Player, lyrics, queue, sleep
npRight.body: From the right: the player to control, meters or lyrics, the queue, the sleep timer, and the settings.

npInfo.title: The track
npInfo.body: Touch the artist or the album to open their page. The bar seeks, the heart saves the track among the favourites, the slider on the right is the volume.

npPanel.title: Meters and animations
npPanel.body: Here live the VU meters, or the animation you chose. The cassette deck and the CD players have working keys: play, stop, skip, eject, the track numbers.

done.title: That is all
done.body: Enjoy the music. You can see this tour again any time from Settings → System info.
